principles: Assess each skill separately: Listening, Reading, Spoken interaction, Spoken production, Writing (and Mediation optionally).
Use at least two tasks per skill and, where possible, two different days, because one performance can mislead.
Judge on what the learner does without unplanned help, not on what they recognise when helped.
Test the level above the suspected one. The learner's level is the highest level at which they perform consistently; failing the next one confirms the ceiling.
Record evidence (note, recording, text sample) with date, task and descriptor IDs.

speaking_level_indicators.typical_failure: Struggles with abstract topics, complex tenses/moods

speaking_level_indicators.vocabulary: Wide in general topics, some in field

speaking_level_indicators.typical_failure: Slips in rare idiom or highly abstract subtlety

diagnostic_task_bank.spoken_interaction: Greet, say name, point to and name 5 objects
diagnostic_task_bank.monologue: Say name and count to ten

diagnostic_task_bank.spoken_interaction: Role-play: introduce yourself and order a coffee
diagnostic_task_bank.reading: Read a menu or notice; answer 3 questions
diagnostic_task_bank.writing: Fill a form; write a postcard (20–30 words)

diagnostic_task_bank.spoken_interaction: Role-play: buy a ticket / ask directions / invite a friend
diagnostic_task_bank.monologue: Tell what you did last weekend and what you will do tomorrow
diagnostic_task_bank.listening: Short announcement or voicemail; extract 3 details
diagnostic_task_bank.reading: Read a timetable, ad or short letter; answer questions
diagnostic_task_bank.writing: Short informal email (40–60 words) about weekend or invitation

diagnostic_task_bank.spoken_interaction: Unprepared conversation about work/hobbies; solve a travel problem (lost luggage)
diagnostic_task_bank.monologue: Narrate a memorable event or the plot of a film with reasons (1–2 min)
diagnostic_task_bank.listening: Radio item on familiar topic; identify main points and some details
diagnostic_task_bank.reading: Newspaper article or blog; main conclusions and details
diagnostic_task_bank.writing: Personal letter or story (100–150 words) describing experience and feelings

diagnostic_task_bank.spoken_interaction: Discussion of a topical issue (advantages/disadvantages); negotiate a solution
diagnostic_task_bank.monologue: Prepared 3-min presentation; defend a viewpoint with examples
diagnostic_task_bank.listening: Lecture or interview; follow argument and speaker attitude
diagnostic_task_bank.reading: Longer article with a viewpoint; infer attitude, summarise
diagnostic_task_bank.writing: Essay or report (200–250 words) with argument for/against

diagnostic_task_bank.spoken_interaction: Abstract debate; role-play a delicate negotiation
diagnostic_task_bank.monologue: 5-min structured talk on complex topic with Q&A
diagnostic_task_bank.listening: Unstructured discussion or documentary with implicit meaning
diagnostic_task_bank.reading: Long literary or specialist text; style and implication
diagnostic_task_bank.writing: Structured, formal essay/report (250–350 words), appropriate register

diagnostic_task_bank.spoken_interaction: Chair a debate; argue subtle positions with irony and allusion
diagnostic_task_bank.monologue: Improvised persuasive speech; defend against hostile questions
diagnostic_task_bank.listening: Fast native speech, mixed accents, humour
diagnostic_task_bank.writing: Synthesis of multiple sources into a polished article; review or critique

decision_rules: Per-skill level: the highest level at which the learner meets most (about 70% or more) of the sampled descriptors across tasks without unplanned help, and does not meet most of the next level.
Plus: meets most descriptors at level L and about half of level L+1 → Lp (A2p, B1p, B2p).
Accuracy check: if range or fluency is one level above accuracy, record the level from accuracy and add a note ("wide but inaccurate").

Overall label (only if needed): the level reached in at least three of the four core skills (listening, reading, speaking [interaction + production combined], writing), with no core skill more than one level below. Otherwise report the profile, not a single label.
Re-test: every 60–120 guided hours, or at end of a course level.
Placement shortcut: start at the suspected level, go up one level after success, down one after failure, stop when a level is passed and the next is failed.
misjudgement_traps: Reading and listening ahead of speaking: do not raise speaking level because of good reading.
Recognition is not production: a learner may understand B1 texts but write A2.
Familiar topics hide the B1 → B2 "abstraction wall": always test an abstract topic at B1+.
Memorised chunks inflate A1–A2: use unprepared questions.
Native-language transfer can make grammar look higher or lower than real (e.g. Romance-language speakers learning Italian/Spanish).
Non-alphabetic or new-script languages: reading/writing may lag far behind speaking at A1s–A2.

by_level.a1: I recognise familiar words and phrases if people speak slowly.
by_level.a2: I understand short clear messages and the main point of everyday talk.
by_level.b1: I follow the main points of clear speech on familiar topics.
by_level.b2: I follow long talks, most news and most films.
by_level.c1: I follow long, unstructured speech and TV without effort.

by_level.a1: I understand names, words and simple sentences on signs and cards.
by_level.a2: I read short simple texts and find specific information.
by_level.b1: I read factual texts and personal letters about familiar topics.
by_level.b2: I read articles with viewpoints and modern fiction.
by_level.c1: I read long, complex texts and notice style.
by_level.c2: I read virtually everything with ease.

by_level.a1: I ask and answer simple questions if the person helps me.
by_level.b1: I cope with most travel situations and join in conversation on familiar topics.
by_level.b2: I speak with enough fluency to talk with native speakers regularly.
by_level.c1: I express myself fluently and flexibly in social and professional life.
by_level.c2: I take part effortlessly in any conversation and convey fine shades of meaning.

by_level.a1: I use simple phrases to say where I live and who I know.
by_level.a2: I describe my family, my daily life and my job in simple terms.
by_level.b1: I tell stories, describe experiences and give reasons for opinions.
by_level.b2: I give detailed presentations and explain a viewpoint.
by_level.c1: I give clear, structured presentations on complex subjects.
by_level.c2: I give smooth, well-organised speeches or arguments for any audience.

by_level.a1: I write a postcard and fill in forms.
by_level.a2: I write short notes and simple personal letters.
by_level.b1: I write connected texts on familiar topics and personal letters.
by_level.b2: I write detailed texts, essays and reports.
by_level.c1: I write well-structured texts on complex subjects.
by_level.c2: I write polished, stylistically appropriate texts of any kind.
